title: Dick and Rick Hoyt Run Together
text:
Rick Hoyt was born in 1962 in Massachusetts with cerebral palsy, after the umbilical cord cut off oxygen to his brain at birth. He could not walk or speak. Doctors advised his parents to place him in an institution. Dick and Judy Hoyt refused. They were convinced he understood everything, and they raised him at home with his brothers.

In 1972 engineers at Tufts University built Rick a computer he could operate with movements of his head, letting him spell out words. Later he went to public school and eventually graduated from Boston University.

In 1977 Rick heard about a five-mile charity race for a young lacrosse player who had been paralyzed in an accident. He told his father he wanted to take part. Dick was not a runner, but he pushed Rick's wheelchair the whole way, and they finished nearly last. Afterward, Rick told his father that when they were running, he felt as if he was not disabled.

That changed both their lives. Team Hoyt went on to complete more than a thousand races together, including the Boston Marathon dozens of times and full Ironman triathlons, in which Dick swam towing Rick in a boat, cycled with him in a special seat and ran pushing his chair. Dick ran his last Boston Marathon with Rick in 2014, at seventy-three. He died in 2021, and Rick two years later.
lesson: A parent's love can turn a child's limits into a shared adventure. Ask what someone wants to do, not only what they cannot.
source: Dick Hoyt with Don Yaeger, Devoted: The Story of a Father's Love for His Son (2010); Boston Athletic Association records
